page: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs running at 3.5 GHz. The CPU features 54 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions, VNNI, and cryptographic instruction sets like AES and SHA-NI. It includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across multi-core compute and high-capacity memory operations. The instance achieved 123,838.97 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 16,462.0 on Geekbench multi-core, placing both metrics in the top 25%. Synthetic tests highlighted top 10% performance in PassMark CPU overall (86,192.71), extended instructions (105,943.53), and encryption (110,183.92). Memory bandwidth reaches 333.99 GB/sec for large block reads and 135.82 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-core metrics fall within average ranges, indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,891.2 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,692.0.

Without local NVMe drives or discrete GPUs, users must evaluate architectural tradeoffs when deploying workloads that depend heavily on hardware accelerators or local disk I/O. For large language model execution, text generation speeds drop sharply on large models, yielding only 2.75 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model. However, prompt processing throughput remains solid on smaller architectures, and memory operations remain competitive, achieving 108.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 70.73 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Qualitatively, the m6i.32xlarge provides high resource density for workloads requiring massive parallelism and high memory footprint without moving to specialized high-memory tiers. The instance profile is optimal for large-scale enterprise applications, high-throughput static web serving, Clang software compilation pipelines, distributed databases, and general caching systems.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory, it maintains a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It provides a 50 Gbps network baseline, while omitting both dedicated local storage and GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, it ranks in the top tier for PassMark CPU multi-threading and encryption, complemented by strong memory bandwidth and high multi-core Clang compilation speeds. While single-thread efficiency and large-model LLM generation remain within median-to-lower percentiles, the 108.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 70.73 GB/sec web serving throughput make it a practical platform for enterprise web applications, in-memory databases, and distributed parallel builds.
